settings.heading: The Hearth and The Moving Day Diagnostic
settings.text: Your grandmother never measured thermal conductivity in Watts per meter-Kelvin. She tapped the rim of the bronze alloy with a wooden ladle, listening for the sustained acoustic decay that proved the casting was free of microscopic voids. She knew the surface was seasoned when the aroma of black mustard seeds bloomed without smoking. In her home, a tava or bell-metal degchi was an Ayurvedic heirloom—seasoned over thirty years, gifted at weddings, and passed down as a sacred instrument. Maison Tavo was born when that heirloom met a modern kitchen move. Unpacking an unlabelled pan, the founder could not determine whether its base would couple with the induction coil or whether its rivets were food-safe tin-bronze. Across seven leading cookware competitors, alloy composition, base mass, and induction compatibility were buried in marketing prose or completely absent. The problem was not a lack of cookware; it was the failure of tools to explain their own construction.

settings.heading: Maison × Tavo
settings.text: “Maison” references the discipline of the French kitchen brigade, Parisian copperware, and Auguste Escoffier’s uncompromising standard of the restaurant pass—where heat is calculated, time is sacred, and every gesture is stripped of ornamentation. “Tavo” preserves an audible, physical link to the tava (तवा) — the ancient round griddle that has anchored Indian hearths and flatbread traditions for three millennia. The synthesis is deliberate: Parisian architectural restraint paired with regional metallurgical heritage. A house where cold-forged precision meets Rajasthan sand-cast bronze.

settings.heading: The Object Before Software
settings.text: We build the physical heirloom first: dual-mass carbon steel that retains thermal energy like cast iron but handles with the agility of cold-rolled sheet; refractory cast clay that breathes with thermal shock resistance; and hand-beaten bell bronze (78% copper, 22% tin) that rings true at 880 Hz. In ancestral Ayurveda, bell metal (kansa) was revered because high-tin bronze is naturally non-reactive to food acids and imparts gentle alkaline balance to slow-simmered dishes. Software, 2D heat simulations, and machine-readable protocols exist solely to serve the physical object, never to replace it.

settings.heading: The Living Pass
settings.text: Between our foundry partners in Rajasthan and our kitchen workshop in London, Maison Tavo operates with the discipline of a restaurant pass. We do not manufacture infinite warehouse inventory on an arbitrary calendar of drops. We open allocations only when a foundry heat is struck, measured, and verified. Each piece carries its serial ledger and metallurgical profile—built not for a season, but to outlast the hand that cooks with it.

settings.heading: The tool that outlasts the hand
settings.lede: Maison Tavo was born from a concrete moment in a working kitchen: the failure of conventional cookware to explain its own metallurgy. We build modern heirlooms for people who cook, and structured specs for machines that assist them.

settings.heading: The Wireframe System
settings.lede: Every surface in Maison Tavo is engineered for both the aesthetic curator and the culinary technologist. Switch between the architectural wireframe screens to inspect how human craft and machine protocols live together.

settings.heading: Specs stay in prose everywhere else
settings.text: Across seven cookware competitors audited on 26 Sep 2026 (Mauviel, Demeyere, HexClad, Our Place, Smithey, Made In, Borough Furnace), material architecture, dimensions, and heat-source compatibility do not appear as structured, agent-parseable fields — only in names, FAQ prose, or description HTML.

settings.heading: Agentic checkout is table stakes
settings.text: HexClad, Our Place, and Smithey already expose full UCP agentic transactions (cart, checkout, payment handlers) via Shopify’s platform default — not as brand-led catalog depth. Buying through an agent is not differentiation; understanding the pan still is.

settings.heading: The open gap is the spec layer
settings.text: Because UCP catalog responses carry no metafields, enrichment must land as JSON-LD additionalProperty on PDPs plus an agent layer that reads the versioned catalog schema directly. That is the surface we are building first.

settings.heading: Why the catalog is machine-readable
settings.lede: Maison Tavo is cookware you can live with and a catalog an agent can reason about. We do not claim to be first in agentic commerce — that bar is already Shopify platform default. The defensible claim: first in cookware to make the product spec layer machine-readable.
settings.closing: Evidence tiers on this page map to the competitor audit in the engagement docs. Dual depth: the curator reads craft and provenance; the technologist reads alloy, heat sources, and structured fields.
